subject: Consolidated: May service economics brief (latency/cost/uptime/usage) — prep for QBR
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Consolidated: May service economics brief (latency/cost/uptime/usage) — prep for QBR

Team,

Attached is the May-service-dashboard.csv with the consolidated latency, cost, uptime, and usage numbers across hosted + dedicated fleets. High level: usage up 18% month-over-month, cost per 1k tokens up ~9% due to fallback quantization on a subset of models, and a small uptick in p95 latency for interactive routes.

We need to consolidate the narrative for Tuesday's QBR. Please do the following by EOD today: 
- Laura: confirm the root causes for the p95 shift (sampled route ids/helpful traces) and produce a very short tech note (1–2 bullets) we can put in the appendix.
- Marcus: validate whether recent autoscaling policy changes could explain the traffic-induced batching differences and provide a mitigation plan (config + rollout timeline).
- Evelyn: draft the top-line exec summary (3 bullets) that ties impact to customers and asks (credits, rollout pause, headcount).

Attachments: May-service-dashboard.csv (attached).

Ask: I want a one-slide narrative: what happened, how we mitigated, what we recommend, and a clear ask for leadership. Keep it crisp.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated: May service economics brief (latency/cost/uptime/usage) — prep for QBR

Diego — quick update after digging in. I attached latency-cost-tradeoffs.pdf with the breakdown and short analysis. Key findings: 

- p50 stable, p95 increased ~120ms (baseline 320ms -> 440ms) only on interactive chat route v3 when batch sizes exceeded 8 requests during peak windows.
- Cost uptick (~9%) correlates with increased fallback to fp16->int8 path when we ran into memory pressure on dedicated nodes (several nodes reported kernel OOM and rolled to safer but less-quantized kernels).
- Uptime: no sustained SLA breaches (99.97% for May), but we did see three transient pod restarts linked to a libcudnn patch mismatch during canary.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Rolled back the libcudnn patch on the affected pool (reduced restarts).
- Tuned the batching cap to 6 for the interactive route during peak window as an emergency measure.

Recommended next steps (for Marcus/infra):
- Short canary (2w) for quantization profile adjustments + node mem tuning.
- Confirm autoscaler thresholds — I suspect we let queue back up which increased batch sizes.

Attachment: latency-cost-tradeoffs.pdf

Summary table (very short):
- Usage: +18% MoM
- Cost/1k tokens: +9% (quantization fallback)
- p95 interactive: +120ms
- Uptime: 99.97%

I flagged the Acme customer impact in the dashboard comments — Sarah from Acme pinged infra and product directly (see cc later).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidated: May service economics brief (latency/cost/uptime/usage) — prep for QBR

Thanks Laura — good catch. Short notes from infra: 

- Autoscaler log shows several windows where target pool size lagged traffic ramp by ~60s; that’s consistent with transient queue growth and larger batches.
- Proposal: implement a temporary lower-burst-threshold and a one-hour fast-scale rule during peak hours (targeting the interactive route only).
- Canary: start a 2-week canary on dedicated pool A with the adjusted quant profile and node mem tuning. Will run synthetic load + shadow traffic from 05/20–06/03.

I’ll open a small runbook for the canary (will link the URL here). Marcus

Diego — I drafted a very short executive summary and attached qbr-exec-summary.txt. Please feel free to trim. Top-line bullets for the QBR slide: 

1) Performance: p95 latency for interactive routes increased by ~120ms in May due to traffic batching and a transient libcudnn canary mismatch; mitigations in place and no sustained customer SLA impact.
2) Economics: unit cost increased ~9% driven by increased fallback to less aggressive quant profiles under memory pressure. We propose a canary + node tuning to recover ~5–7% of the delta.
3) Ask: approval for a 2-week canary on dedicated pool A, one-time customer credits for materially impacted accounts (recommendation: small credit for Acme), and prioritization of the quota/autoscale follow-up in infra backlog.

If Diego approves, I’ll add the 1-slide summary to the QBR deck and include the two-page appendix (Laura’s notes + Marcus’ canary runbook link).

Evelyn Hart
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference
